title: Microburst NaN bisect journal
content:
Quick log of an intermittent NaN (microburst) observed when switching from bf16 to int8/FP8 on the 13B LLM variant. This is my personal bisect/notes file — messy, chronological, hypotheses and commands I ran so far.

Observation:
- Model produces valid outputs under bf16 99% of the time; after enabling per-channel int8 or FP8 quant path for attention + FFN, we see a tiny fraction (~0.04%) of requests return tensors with NaNs in logits or loss=nan during evaluation. Usually happens within first 30 tokens. Unreliable, hard to reproduce locally.

Initial reproducer attempts (local):
- baseline (bf16): python run_inference.py --model 13B --dtype bf16 --batch 1 --prompt "def foo"
  -> stable, no NaN.
- int8 path (per-channel symmetric): python run_inference.py --model 13B --quant int8 --batch 1 --prompt "def foo"
  -> random NaN after 12-20 runs.
- fp8-e4m3: python run_inference.py --model 13B --quant fp8 --format e4m3 --batch 1 --prompt "def foo"
  -> similar flaky NaN.

Exact error snippets captured (some vary):
- "RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered"
- "AssertionError: allclose failed (found nan)"
- "NaN encountered in logits at token idx 17"
- stack snippet: at rw_runtime/kernels/attention.cu: line 241 -> compute_softmax -> sum becomes inf/nan

What I tried (and results):
1) Reduce batch size to 1 (already 1) — no change.
2) Disable fused kernels for attention and gelu: set env RW_DISABLE_FUSED=1 and re-run -> vastly fewer NaNs, but still seen in one run out of ~200. Suggests fused kernel may be contributing but not solely responsible.
3) Turn off autotuning/cuBLAS heuristics: export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8; export CUBLAS_LOGINFO_DBG=1 -> inconclusive.
4) Switch to deterministic math on matmul path: torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high') and set TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=0 -> slight improvement.
5) Try BF16 for LayerNorm and attention softmax but int8 elsewhere: created hybrid path where layernorm ops forced to bf16 via dtype override -> seems to remove NaNs locally (3/3 runs), indicates LayerNorm precision could be fragile.
6) KV cache corruption hypothesis: instrumented KV dump after each layer into /tmp/kv_dumps (binary) and diffed between good/bad runs -> first divergence at layer 7 (attention output shows NaN).
7) Gradient vs inference: verified this happens in inference only (no backward).
8) Rebuilt runtime with bounds-checking in attention kernel (cheap mod) to log sum and max values before softmax -> caught a case where pre-softmax logits had large values (~1e5) due to accumulation overflow in int32 accumulator when using quant-dequant path in fused kernel.

Hypotheses so far:
- H1: Quantization scale overflow in int8/FP8 path. Per-channel scale computed from calibration can be too small, causing enormous dequantized values after multiplying by inverse_scale. Edge-case outlier input token/embedding causing large accumulation.
- H2: Accumulator precision mismatch. Fused kernel uses int32 accumulator, but quantization/dequant ordering + reorder/transpose could overflow before reduce to float.
- H3: LayerNorm/softmax precision interaction. If variance estimate is computed in low precision near-zero, dividing leads to inf/nan. For fp8 path, the dynamic range hit boundary condition.
- H4: Race/unaligned memory write in optimized fused kernel when sequence length short leads to stale values in KV memory. The KV dump divergence suggests corruption location near attention output.

Additional commands / debug flags used:
- run with RW_INSTRUMENT_KV=1 to dump per-layer kvs.
- LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/libjemalloc.so GDB run minimal example to watch tensor memory. (GDB not great with CUDA kernels.)
- Set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to force synchronous launches and get better tracebacks.
- Built a special debug binary with -DRW_CHECK_NAN_ON_WRITE to assert if any store writes NaN. This triggered at fused_attention_forward in one run.

Notes from PR/issue cross-references:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/482 (attempted safer dequant sequence; author: @ethanb)
- Jira: INF-2345 (NaN on quantized path) — has some telemetry logs from production showing identical pattern: failure peaks at 03:00 UTC, correlated with short sequences coming from a specific customer template.

Quick experiments to try next (TODOs):
- Recompute per-channel scales with robust outlier clipping (e.g., 99.9 percentile) and run 10k requests in local fuzzing harness.
- Force LayerNorm ops to fp32 (not only bf16) temporarily to rule out variance calculation precision.
- Add saturation clamp after dequant multiply before accumulation to avoid blowing up sums.
- Add Canary test: fuzz prompts of varied tokenization lengths including odd emojis / rare tokens that produced spikes in PR logs.
- Re-run with RW_DISABLE_FUSED=1 across Dedicated pool for a day to see production impact.
- Add telemetry: log max pre-softmax value per request (sampled 1%) to identify upstream triggers.

Questions I want to answer in next session:
- Is the failure deterministic for certain token sequences (likely yes given INF-2345 correlation)? If so, can we extract minimal token subsequence that triggers large pre-softmax values?
- Is dequant scaling computed per-tensor during runtime or baked into the quantized checkpoint? If runtime, where is precision/overflow handled?
- Could recent kernel rewrite (commit 9f2cb4) have introduced an unaligned write? Quick bisect candidate: revert that commit and rerun fuzz harness.

Random breadcrumbs/notes:
- Observed one stack with cuDNN call returning CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM — maybe unrelated but worth flagging to infra.
- Customer temporary mitigation: pin to bf16. Ops team asked for rollback window.
- I pushed a small logging change on PR draft (wip/log-pre-softmax) to capture top-3 pre-softmax values into runtime trace logs for production sampling.

Chronology snippets (most recent first):
- 2026-02-28 14:12 — caught a NaN in prod under canary. Logged pre-softmax and KV checksum.
- 2026-02-25 09:04 — local run: forced fp32 LN -> no NaNs in 200 runs.
- 2026-01-10 — initial report by SRE (INF-2345), roughly started bisecting.

If anyone (Ethan, Marco, or SREs) reads this: please add any stray stack traces or sample prompts into the INF-2345 ticket. I will try the robust-scale + clamp path next and run the 50k request fuzz harness overnight.

End of scratchpad for now. Will copy important findings into INF-2345 and link PR once I have deterministic minimal repro.
